mainTopic: Family riddles, and whether brothers who converted or were freed together may marry each other's wives
overview: The amud opens with riddles about strange family relationships. In the first, a woman's half brother is married to her mother, and רמי בר חמא notes this works only according to the רבנן of our משנה, not רבי יהודה. More riddles follow. Most are solved by a גוי who lived with a close relative, but the cousin riddle can happen through permitted marriages. Then a new משנה teaches that sons who converted with their mother, or were freed with her, do not do חליצה or יבום for each other's wives. In the גמרא, רב אחא בר יעקב lets freed brothers marry each other's wives, while רב ששת forbids it. The גמרא defines their dispute in two versions, then tests רב אחא's view against the משנה and its word 'אפילו', which turns out to fit either side. Finally it brings a ברייתא about twin converts, and its inference continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The riddle of the half brother who married my mother
steps.stepSummary: A woman says her father's son, who is not her mother's son, is married to her mother, so she is his wife's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: "I have a brother from my father but not from my mother. He is my mother's husband, and I am his wife's daughter."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a riddle a woman says about her own family. It sets up the next step, where רמי בר חמא explains which opinion allows this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is how it works. A man raped or seduced a woman without marrying her, and she had a daughter. His son from a different woman later married that same woman. So the daughter's half brother on her father's side is now her mother's husband. This relies on the משנה's ruling that a son may marry his father's אנוסה or מפותה.

keyTerms.meaning: A brother from the father's side only (a paternal half brother)
Her daughter (here: the daughter of his wife)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the half brother married his own mother. The woman he married is the speaker's mother, and she was never married to his father.

phrases.english: "A brother from the father and not from the mother,
and he is the husband of the mother,
and I am the daughter of his wife."

steps.triggerLanguage: אַח מֵאַב וְלֹא מֵאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's ruling that a man may marry his father's אנוסה or מפותה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A family can exist where a woman's paternal half brother is married to her mother.

steps.title: This case does not work according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says the riddle's case only works according to the רבנן of our משנה, not according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: This is not like the opinion of רבי יהודה in our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא points out that the first riddle depends on a disagreement in our משנה. It only works according to one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids a son from marrying a woman his father raped or seduced. According to him, the half brother could never marry the speaker's mother, so the riddle could not happen. Only the רבנן, who allow such a marriage, make this family possible.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who comments on the riddle
Not in line with רבי יהודה's opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a strange-sounding riddle is really a practical result of a halachic disagreement about marrying one's father's אנוסה or מפותה.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
This is not according to Rabbi Yehuda of our mishna.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which opinion in the משנה makes the riddle of step 1 possible.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The riddle in step 1 works only according to the רבנן, not according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The riddle of the child who is both brother and son
steps.stepSummary: A woman carrying a child says he is both her brother and her son. The answer is a גוי who lived with his own daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He is my brother and he is my son. I am the sister of this one I carry on my shoulders." You find this in a גוי who lived with his daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second family riddle and then its solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גוי has a son with his own daughter, that boy shares a father with her, so he is her brother. She also gave birth to him, so he is her son. The גמרא sets the case with a גוי because it does not want to picture a Jew acting this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom I carry on my shoulders
You find it (here is the solution)
A gentile who lived with his own daughter

phrases.english: "He is a brother, and he is my son,
I am the sister
of this one whom I carry on my shoulders" —
you find it
in a gentile who engaged in intercourse with his daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָח הוּא וּבְרִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second family riddle to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child born to a גוי and his daughter is both her brother and her son.

steps.title: The riddle of the mother who is her son's niece
steps.stepSummary: A woman greets her son and says she is his sister's daughter. The answer is a גוי who lived with his daughter's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Peace to you, my son; I am your sister's daughter." You find this in a גוי who lived with his daughter's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third riddle and its solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי has a son with his granddaughter, his daughter's daughter. The boy's father is the גוי, so the גוי's daughter is the boy's half sister. The boy's mother is that daughter's daughter, so she is his sister's daughter as well as his mother.

phrases.english: "Peace to you, my son,
I am the daughter of your sister" —

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּגוֹי הַבָּא עַל בַּת בִּתּוֹ.
phrases.english: you find it in a gentile who engaged in intercourse with the daughter of his daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלָמָא לָךְ בְּרִי בַּת אֲחָתִיךְ אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 3, one generation further down through a daughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child born to a גוי and his daughter's daughter is the son of his own sister's daughter.

steps.title: The water drawers' riddle: my son, and I am his brother's daughter
steps.stepSummary: A woman calls out to water drawers with a puzzle: the boy she carries is her son, and she is his brother's daughter. The answer is a גוי who lived with his son's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Water drawers drawing with buckets, let a hard riddle fall among you: this one I carry is my son, and I am his brother's daughter." You find this in a גוי who lived with his son's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fourth riddle, along with its solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי has a son with his granddaughter, his son's daughter. The baby's father is the גוי, so the גוי's son is the baby's half brother. The mother is that son's daughter, so she is the baby's brother's daughter as well as his mother. It is the same idea as step 4, only through the son instead of the daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: A hidden riddle, hard to unlock

steps.whatToRemember: The riddles in steps 3-5 turn on one idea: when a man has a child with a close relative, the child ends up related to its own mother in two ways at once. The first riddle also shows a real halachic point, since it only works according to the רבנן who allow marrying a father's אנוסה or מפותה.

phrases.english: "Water drawers who draw with buckets,
let a cryptic riddle fall among you:
phrases.notes: Literally "closed and open," meaning a puzzle that needs solving.

phrases.english: this one whom I carry is a son,
and I am the daughter of his brother" —

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּגוֹי הַבָּא עַל בַּת בְּנוֹ.
phrases.english: you find it in a gentile who engaged in intercourse with the daughter of his son.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּלָּאֵי דְּדָלוּ דַּוְולָא לִיפּוֹל בְּכוּ סְתַר פְּתַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror case of step 4: a granddaughter through a son instead of a daughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child born to a גוי and his son's daughter is the son of his own brother's daughter.

steps.title: The 'woe for my brother' riddle
steps.stepSummary: A woman mourns a man who is her brother, father, husband, her husband's son and her mother's husband, and who will not feed his orphan brothers, who are also his grandsons. The answer is a גוי who lived with his mother and then with the daughter born from that union, and his old father also lived with that daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Woe, woe for my brother, who is my father, my husband, the son of my husband and the husband of my mother. I am the daughter of his wife, and he won't give bread to his orphan brothers, who are his daughter's sons." Answer: a גוי lived with his mother and had a daughter. Then he lived with that daughter. Then his old father also lived with her and had sons with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another family riddle and solves it with a case of a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter's mother is the man's own mother, so he is both her brother and her father. He lived with her, so he is her husband. His father, the old man, also had her, so the man is also her husband's son. Her sons from the old man are the man's brothers and also his daughter's sons, and they are orphans because the old man has died.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can find it': the formula that gives the solution to a case
The old man; here, the גוי's father

phrases.english: "Woe, woe for my brother,
who is my father, and who is my husband,
and who is the son of my husband,
and who is the husband of my mother,
and I am the daughter of his wife,
phrases.notes: 'His wife' is his own mother, since he lived with her.

phrases.english: and he does not give bread
to his brothers, the orphans, the sons of his daughter."
You find it in the case of a gentile

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא עַל אִמּוֹ וְהוֹלִיד מִמֶּנָּה בַּת,
phrases.english: who lived with his mother and fathered a daughter from her,
and then he lived with that daughter,
and then the old man lived with her
phrases.notes: The old man is the גוי's own father.

phrases.english: and fathered sons from her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּגוֹי הַבָּא עַל אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another riddle in the same series, solved the same way, with forbidden relations among גוים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The riddle works when a גוי fathers a daughter with his mother, lives with that daughter, and his father also has sons with her.

steps.title: The 'we are all siblings' riddle
steps.stepSummary: A woman tells a boy that she is the sibling of him, of his father and of his mother. The answer is a גוי who fathered two daughters with his mother, then had a son with one of them. The other daughter says this to the boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You and I are siblings, your father and I are siblings, your mother and I are siblings." Answer: a גוי lived with his mother and had two daughters. He then had a son with one daughter, and the other daughter, the boy's aunt, calls to him and says this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another riddle and solves it with a גוי who lived with his mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The speaker has the same father as the boy, so they are siblings. She has the same mother as the boy's father, so she is his father's sister. She has the same father and mother as the boy's mother, so she is his mother's sister.

phrases.english: "You and I are siblings,
your father and I are siblings,
your mother and I are siblings."

phrases.aramaic: — מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּגוֹי הַבָּא עַל אִמּוֹ
phrases.english: You find it in a gentile who lived with his mother
and fathered two daughters from her,
and then he lived with one of them,
and fathered a son from her,
and the sister of the boy's mother calls to him
and says this to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ בְּגוֹי הַבָּא עַל אִמּוֹ וְהוֹלִיד מִמֶּנָּה שְׁתֵּי בָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of riddles solved through a גוי's forbidden relations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The riddle works with a גוי who has two daughters with his mother and a son with one of those daughters.

steps.title: The cousins riddle, which works with permitted marriages
steps.stepSummary: A boy tells another boy that he is cousin to him, to his father and to his mother. The גמרא notes that this one can be solved with permitted marriages: ראובן's two daughters marry his brother שמעון and the son of his brother לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You and I are cousins, your father and I are cousins, your mother and I are cousins." This one can even happen in a permitted way. ראובן has two daughters. שמעון marries one, and לוי's son marries the other. שמעון's son says this to לוי's grandson.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a final riddle and points out that it does not need forbidden relations at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two boys' mothers are sisters, so the boys are cousins. שמעון and לוי are brothers, so שמעון's son is cousin to לוי's son, the other boy's father. שמעון and ראובן are brothers, so שמעון's son is also cousin to ראובן's daughter, the other boy's mother.
steps.whatToRemember: The first riddles needed forbidden relations among גוים. The cousin riddle is different, because it can happen through normal, permitted marriages.

phrases.english: "You and I are cousins,
your father and I are cousins,
your mother and I are cousins."
This one you can find in a permitted way as well:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן רְאוּבֵן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי בָנוֹת,
phrases.english: for example, Reuven, who has two daughters,
and Shimon came and married one of them,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא בַּר לֵוִי וּנְסַב חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: and Levi's son came and married the other one,
and Shimon's son says it
to Levi's grandson.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בְּהֶיתֵּירָא נָמֵי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the riddle series with one that does not need forbidden relations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cousin riddle can be solved with permitted marriages among three brothers' families.

steps.title: New משנה: brothers who converted with their mother do not do יבום
steps.stepSummary: A גיורת whose sons converted with her: the sons do not do חליצה or יבום for each other's wives. This holds even when the first son was conceived before she converted and born after, and the second was conceived and born after. The same applies to a שפחה whose sons were freed with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A female convert whose sons converted with her: they do not do חליצה and they do not do יבום. This is true even if the first son was conceived before she converted and born after, while the second son was conceived and born after she converted. The same is true for a שפחה whose sons were freed together with her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules that sons of a גיורת or a freed שפחה are not counted as brothers for יבום or חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום applies only between brothers who share a father. A convert is treated like a newborn, so the family ties from before his conversion do not count for this. Even the case where one son was fully born Jewish does not change the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: His conception and birth were in holiness, after the mother became Jewish

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the second son, who was born fully Jewish, changes things. The משנה says 'even' to stress that the brothers still do no יבום or חליצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next סוגיא about how far a convert's earlier family ties count in הלכה.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A female convert
whose sons converted along with her:
they do not perform חליצה and do not perform יבום,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִלּוּ הוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
phrases.english: even if the conception of the first was not in holiness
phrases.notes: 'In holiness' means after the mother had already become Jewish.

phrases.english: but his birth was in holiness,
and the second was both conceived and born in holiness.
And the same applies to a maidservant whose sons were freed along with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַגִּיּוֹרֶת שֶׁנִּתְגַּיְּירוּ בָּנֶיהָ עִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the riddles end, a new משנה opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sons who converted with their mother, or were freed with her, do not do יבום or חליצה for each other, even if one of them was born Jewish.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב permits יודן's freed sons to marry each other's wives
steps.stepSummary: A real case: the sons of a freed שפחה named יודן were freed, and רב אחא בר יעקב allowed them to marry each other's wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of יודן the maidservant were freed. רב אחא בר יעקב allowed them to marry each other's wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a real story. רב אחא בר יעקב allowed freed brothers to marry each other's wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that freed brothers do not do יבום or חליצה, because legally they are not related. רב אחא takes this one step further. Since they are not related, one brother may even marry the other's wife.

phrases.english: GEMARA
The sons of Yudan the maidservant were freed

phrases.aramaic: שְׁרָא לְהוּ רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov permitted them
to marry each other's wives

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי יוּדָן אַמְתָּא אִשְׁתַּחְרוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's rule about freed brothers (step 9) to a real case and extends it to marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Freed brothers may marry each other's wives (according to רב אחא בר יעקב).

steps.title: רבא objects: רב ששת forbade this
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב אחא by pointing out that רב ששת had forbidden this exact thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But רב ששת forbade it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב אחא's ruling by quoting an opposing ruling from רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge comes from authority, not from a פסוק or a ברייתא. רב ששת had already ruled that this is forbidden, so how could רב אחא permit it?

phrases.english: Rava said to him
But Rav Sheshet forbade it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָסַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's permission for the freed brothers to marry each other's wives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier authority, רב ששת, ruled the opposite.

steps.title: רב אחא answers: he forbids and I permit
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא answers that he simply disagrees with רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He forbids it, and I permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא answers that he knows about רב ששת's ruling and does not agree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא does not try to reconcile the two rulings. He openly takes the other side of a dispute. This sets up the גמרא's next question: what exactly are they arguing about?

phrases.english: He said to him
He forbids, and I permit

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אָסַר וַאֲנָא שָׁרֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Open disagreement: the challenge is accepted as a real dispute, not resolved.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אחא's ruling cannot stand against רב ששת's.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a real מחלוקת between רב אחא and רב ששת.

steps.title: Where everyone agrees: paternal brothers permitted, maternal brothers forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the limits of the dispute. Brothers only from the father are permitted by all, and brothers only from the mother are forbidden by all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they are brothers from the father and not from the mother, everyone agrees it is permitted. If they are brothers from the mother and not from the father, everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks off the cases where there is no argument. This prepares for the next step, which shows exactly where the dispute lies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave or גוי has no legally recognized connection to his father, so paternal brothers are clearly strangers and everyone permits. A mother is always known, so people see maternal brothers as real brothers. Everyone forbids that case, so people won't think a man may marry his brother's wife.
steps.confusionAlert: Freed maternal brothers are not truly related according to the תורה. The prohibition here is only because of how it looks to people.

phrases.english: From the father and not from the mother
everyone agrees that it is permitted
From the mother and not from the father
everyone agrees that it is forbidden

steps.triggerLanguage: מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the scope of the dispute revealed in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Paternal-only brothers: permitted by all. Maternal-only brothers: forbidden by all.

steps.title: The real dispute: brothers from both parents
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is about brothers from both father and mother. One side says people identify them by their father. רב ששת says they are also called by their mother's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree when the brothers share both father and mother. The one who permits says we follow the father, since people call them 'the sons of so-and-so' (the father). רב ששת holds that people also call them 'the sons of so-and-so' (the mother).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pinpoints the case in dispute and gives each side's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is which family name people use for these brothers. If they are known by their father's name, everyone treats them as unrelated, so there is nothing confusing about the marriage. If they are also known by their mother's name, people will see them as brothers, so רב ששת forbids, just as in the maternal-only case.

keyTerms.meaning: We place them after the father (identify them by the father)

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole dispute turns on public perception: how people refer to these brothers decides whether the marriage looks like marrying a brother's wife.

phrases.english: When they disagree
it is from the father and from the mother
The one who permits
we trace them after the father
since they are called 'the sons of so-and-so'
And Rav Sheshet
they are also called 'the sons of so-and-so'
phrases.notes: This time the name is the mother's, so people see them as maternal brothers too.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי מִן הָאָב וּמִן הָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having set aside the agreed cases in step 13, this step names the disputed case and the reasoning behind each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For full brothers: רב אחא permits because they are known by their father; רב ששת forbids because they are also known by their mother.
steps.whatToRemember: Under this first version, the dispute is only about full brothers. Paternal-only brothers are permitted by everyone, and maternal-only brothers are forbidden by everyone.

steps.title: Second version: רב אחא permits even maternal brothers
steps.stepSummary: Another version says רב אחא בר יעקב permits even maternal brothers, because a גר who converted is like a newborn child.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב אחא בר יעקב disagrees even about brothers from the mother. What is the reason? A convert who has converted is like a newborn child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the dispute. In this version, רב אחא is more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב אחא is not worried about how it looks at all. Since a גר is legally a brand-new person, all his old family ties are gone, even through the mother. So according to him, the maternal-only case is permitted too.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert is like a newborn child

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions. In the first, the dispute is only about full brothers. In the second, רב אחא permits even maternal brothers, because a גר is like a newborn.

phrases.english: And some say
Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov disagrees
even regarding brothers from the mother
And what is the reason?
A convert who converted
is like a child just born

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמַר פְּלִיג רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the dispute that widens it beyond the limits set in steps 13-14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב אחא בר יעקב, even maternal brothers who converted or were freed may marry each other's wives, since a גר is like a newborn.

steps.title: The משנה about a convert and her sons seems to forbid them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה saying that sons who converted with their mother do not do חליצה or יבום. It suggests the reason is that they are forbidden to each other's wives, which goes against רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: a woman convert whose sons converted with her — they do not do חליצה and they do not do יבום. What is the reason? Isn't it because they are forbidden to each other's wives?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to contradict רב אחא בר יעקב, who permitted maternal brothers who converted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's brothers converted together with their mother. If the משנה says no יבום because the wives are forbidden to them, then their family tie still counts after conversion, and רב אחא's permission seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who converted to Judaism
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
Levirate marriage: a man marries his brother's childless widow

phrases.english: We learned: a female convert whose sons converted with her —
they do not do חליצה and do not do יבום.
What is the reason? Is it not because they are forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא, לָאו מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲסִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's permission (steps 10-15) from the wording of our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's ruling that brothers who converted (or were freed) together may marry each other's wives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says no יבום. The most natural reason is that the wives are forbidden to the brothers, so the maternal tie still counts.

steps.title: No יבום means the wives are free, not forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה only means יבום does not apply here. The widow may marry anyone, including the brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means she is not under the law of חליצה and יבום, so she is permitted to marry anyone. And they are also permitted to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אחא by reading the משנה differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No חליצה and no יבום' does not have to mean 'forbidden.' It can mean the brothers are not legally brothers, so the whole יבום system does not apply. The widow is a free woman, and the brothers may marry her like anyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Under the law of / included in the category of

steps.confusionAlert: 'No יבום' does not always mean the widow is forbidden. Here it means יבום simply does not apply, so she is fully free, even to the brothers.

phrases.english: No, it means she is not under the law of חליצה and יבום,
and she is permitted to anyone.
And they too are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּאֵינָהּ בְּתוֹרַת חֲלִיצָה וְיִיבּוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No יבום because the wives are forbidden to the brothers.
steps.terutzMaskana: No יבום because the brothers are not legally related. The wife is free to marry anyone, including them.

steps.title: The word 'אפילו' in the משנה fits better with forbidding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the word 'אפילו' (even) in the משנה. It fits nicely if the brothers are forbidden, but seems to have no point if they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'even'! If you say they are forbidden, that explains 'even': even though the first son was conceived before his mother converted and born after, while the second was conceived and born after, so they are like sons of two different mothers, they are still forbidden. But if you say they are permitted, what does 'even' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 17 using the word 'אפילו' from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה continues with 'even' a case where one son was conceived before the conversion and one after. That case looks like two separate mothers, so the bigger news would be that they are still forbidden. If they are permitted anyway, the case is not surprising, so 'even' seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Even (a word showing a surprising case)
In holiness, meaning after the mother converted
It makes sense if you say...

phrases.english: But it teaches 'even',
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: 'even if the first was conceived before conversion and born after, and the second was conceived and born after.'

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say they are forbidden,
that is why it teaches 'even' —

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּרִאשׁוֹן הוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
phrases.english: that although the first was conceived not in holiness
and born in holiness,
and the second was conceived and born in holiness,
so they are like sons of two mothers,
even so — they are forbidden.
But if you say they are permitted, what is 'even'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָתָנֵי אֲפִילּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of step 17 using the משנה's own wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the brothers are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Even' introduces the surprising case. A ruling to forbid is surprising in the 'two mothers' case. A ruling to permit there is expected, so 'even' would be pointless.

steps.title: 'אפילו' means permitted even though people might confuse them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains 'even' in a way that fits permitting. Both sons were born after the conversion, so people might think they are regular Jewish brothers. Even so, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Although both of them were born in holiness, and people might mix them up with regular Jews, even so they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 18 by finding a different 'surprise' in the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is the danger of confusion, not the 'two mothers' angle. Both sons were born as Jews, so onlookers might think they are ordinary Jewish brothers, who may not marry a brother's wife except through יבום. The משנה says that even with this risk, they are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: To be confused or mixed up

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ לֵידָתָן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
phrases.english: That although both of them were born in holiness,
and people may come to confuse them with Jews,
phrases.notes: Meaning born-Jewish brothers, who may not marry each other's wives outside of יבום.

phrases.english: even so — it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ לֵידָתָן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Even' only makes sense if the brothers are forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Even' means permitted, despite the risk that people will confuse them with born Jews.

steps.title: Another version: the word 'אפילו' actually proves they are permitted
steps.stepSummary: Another version says the word 'even' itself supports permitting. 'Even' fits the idea of 'permitted despite possible confusion.' If they were forbidden, the word would have no point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: it also makes sense that they are permitted, because it says 'even.' If you say they are permitted, that explains 'even': although both were born in holiness and people may confuse them with Jews, even so they are permitted. But if you say they are forbidden, what is 'even'?
steps.whatsHappening: This version turns the same word 'אפילו' into a proof for רב אחא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version starts from the claim that the surprise in 'even' is the risk of confusion with born Jews, and that point only fits a ruling to permit. So the word looks like support for permitting, and a ruling to forbid would seem to leave 'even' with no meaning. The next step shows the forbidding view can still explain 'even'.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (another version)
It is also logical this way

steps.whatToRemember: The word 'אפילו' in the משנה can be read both ways. In the first version it looked like a problem for רב אחא and was answered. In the second version it is offered as a proof for him, but the next step shows it also fits the forbidding view, so it proves nothing either way.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
So too it is logical that they are permitted,
since it teaches 'even'.
It makes sense if you say they are permitted —
that is why it teaches 'even',

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ לֵידָתָן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
phrases.english: that although both of them were born in holiness,
so people may come to confuse them with Jews —
even so they are permitted.
But if you say they are forbidden, what is 'even'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא דִּשְׁרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of steps 18-19. The word 'אפילו' becomes a proof instead of a challenge.
steps.raayaObject: רב אחא בר יעקב's view that converted maternal brothers are permitted to each other's wives
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'אפילו' in the משנה of הגיורת שנתגיירו בניה עמה

steps.title: The word 'even' also fits the view that they are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that 'אפילו' makes sense even if the brothers are forbidden. One son was conceived before the conversion and the other after, so they seem like sons of two different mothers. Even so, they are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה means this: the first son was conceived before his mother converted and born after, while the second son was both conceived and born after she converted. So they look like sons of two different mothers. Even so, they are forbidden to marry each other's wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 20 by showing that the word 'אפילו' also has a clear point if the brothers are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 claimed that 'even' only makes sense if the brothers are permitted. Here the גמרא gives a reading where 'even' fits forbidding. Since the two sons began life in different states, one might think they are like strangers from two mothers. The משנה says that even so, they are forbidden. The word 'even' therefore proves nothing either way.

keyTerms.meaning: In holiness, meaning after the mother became Jewish

steps.confusionAlert: 'Conceived in holiness' does not mean anything mystical. It just means the mother was already Jewish when the baby was conceived.

phrases.english: That even though the first son
was conceived not in holiness
phrases.notes: Meaning he was conceived while his mother was not yet Jewish.

phrases.english: and his birth was in holiness,
and the second was both conceived and born in holiness,
so that they are like sons of two mothers
even so, they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּרִאשׁוֹן הוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּקְדוּשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20's claim by showing that 'even' also fits the forbidding view.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the word 'אפילו' as support for permitting.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'even' has no point if they are forbidden. In fact it can mean 'forbidden even though they seem like sons of two mothers.'

steps.title: A ברייתא about twin brothers who converted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three cases of twin brothers: converted after they were already born, conceived before but born after the conversion, and conceived and born after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: twin brothers who converted, and also twins who were freed slaves, do not do חליצה or יבום, and they are not liable for a brother's wife. If they were conceived before their mother converted but born after, they do not do חליצה or יבום, but they are liable for a brother's wife. If they were conceived and born after the conversion, they are like regular Jews in every way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof by quoting a ברייתא. It is setting up a challenge that it will draw out in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three levels. Converts who were already born count as having no family ties, so there is no יבום and no punishment for a brother's wife. Twins born after the conversion have a mother relationship, so a brother's wife is forbidden to them, but they still have no יבום because יבום depends on the father. Twins conceived and born after the conversion are like any Jewish brothers.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Two twin brothers who are converts,
and likewise twins who are freed slaves
do not do חליצה and do not do יבום,
and they are not liable for a brother's wife.
If they were conceived not in holiness
and born in holiness
they do not do חליצה and do not do יבום,
but they are liable for a brother's wife.
If they were conceived and born in holiness
they are like regular Jews in all their matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁנֵי אַחִים תְּאוֹמִים גֵּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the argument over 'אפילו' ends without a proof, the גמרא brings a new source about the same question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's view that converted brothers may marry each other's wives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's wording about converted twins will be used to show that some prohibition still exists.

steps.title: Reading closely: only 'no liability' for convert twins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא focuses on the ברייתא's words 'not liable for a brother's wife' and starts to infer that only punishment is missing. The thought continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches that convert twins are not liable for a brother's wife. This means there is no liability for punishment...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is drawing an inference from the ברייתא's exact words. This step is unfinished and sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא did not say convert twins are 'permitted.' It only said they are 'not liable.' The גמרא is starting to argue that no punishment does not mean no prohibition at all. That would challenge רב אחא בר יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches (points to the key line)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not liable' is not the same as 'permitted.' The גמרא is about to use that difference.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
they are not liable for a brother's wife,
so there is no liability

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי מִיהַת: אֵין חַיָּיבִין מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks out the key words of the ברייתא from Step 22 to build the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's view that converted brothers are fully permitted to each other's wives.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says only 'no liability,' which suggests a lesser prohibition may still exist. This argument is completed in the next section.
